civilizations.name: Mesopotamian Civilizations
civilizations.description: The civilizations of Mesopotamia developed between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers and became some of the earliest urban societies in human history.
civilizations.legacy: Mesopotamian societies made foundational contributions to writing, law, urban life, mathematics and organized government.

civilizations.name: Ancient Egypt
civilizations.description: Ancient Egypt developed along the Nile and created one of the world's most enduring civilizations, famous for monumental architecture, writing and royal traditions.
civilizations.legacy: Egyptian architecture, art, writing and cultural traditions remain central to the study of ancient history.

civilizations.name: Indus Valley Civilization
civilizations.description: The Indus Valley Civilization developed in parts of South Asia and is known for carefully planned cities, drainage systems, craft production and long-distance trade.
civilizations.legacy: The Indus Valley Civilization is fundamental to the study of early South Asian urbanism and archaeology.

civilizations.name: Ancient Chinese Civilizations
civilizations.description: Ancient Chinese civilization developed through successive dynasties and created important traditions in government, philosophy, writing, technology and art.
civilizations.legacy: Chinese political philosophy, writing, art, technology and cultural traditions have had an enormous historical influence.

civilizations.name: Ancient Greece
civilizations.description: Ancient Greek societies developed independent city-states and produced influential traditions in philosophy, politics, science, literature, architecture and art.
civilizations.legacy: Greek intellectual and artistic traditions strongly influenced later European and Mediterranean societies.

civilizations.name: Roman Civilization
civilizations.description: Rome grew from a city-state into a vast republic and empire whose institutions, infrastructure, law and culture shaped much of Europe and the Mediterranean.
civilizations.legacy: Roman law, languages, architecture, infrastructure and political ideas remain deeply important to world history.

civilizations.name: Persian Empires
civilizations.description: Persian empires created large and diverse political systems across western and central Asia and developed sophisticated administrative traditions.
civilizations.legacy: Persian political, artistic and cultural traditions played a major role in the history of the ancient Near East.

civilizations.name: Maya Civilization
civilizations.description: Maya civilization developed across parts of Mesoamerica and became known for cities, mathematics, astronomy, writing and monumental architecture.
civilizations.legacy: Maya intellectual and architectural achievements remain an important part of the history of the Americas.

civilizations.name: Inca Civilization
civilizations.description: The Inca developed a large Andean state with sophisticated administration, roads, agriculture and monumental construction.
civilizations.legacy: Inca engineering and Andean cultural traditions remain major subjects of archaeology and history.

civilizations.name: Aztec Civilization
civilizations.description: The Aztec Empire developed in central Mexico and built a powerful political and economic center around Tenochtitlan.
civilizations.legacy: Aztec history remains important to the understanding of pre-Columbian Mesoamerica.

civilizations.name: Byzantine Civilization
civilizations.description: The Byzantine Empire continued many Roman political and cultural traditions while developing a distinctive Greek-speaking Christian civilization centered on Constantinople.
civilizations.legacy: Byzantine traditions influenced Eastern Europe, Christianity, art, architecture and preservation of classical learning.

civilizations.name: Islamic Golden Age
civilizations.description: The Islamic Golden Age saw major developments in mathematics, medicine, astronomy, philosophy, geography and literature across a wide connected world.
civilizations.legacy: Its scholarship helped preserve, develop and transmit knowledge across civilizations.

civilizations.name: Khmer Civilization
civilizations.description: The Khmer Empire became a major Southeast Asian civilization known for monumental architecture, water management and the city of Angkor.
civilizations.legacy: Khmer architecture and Angkor remain among the most significant cultural achievements of Southeast Asia.

civilizations.name: Mesoamerican Civilizations
civilizations.description: Mesoamerica was home to interconnected civilizations with rich traditions in agriculture, architecture, writing, astronomy, trade and political organization.
civilizations.legacy: Mesoamerican civilizations created some of the most important urban and intellectual traditions of pre-Columbian America.

civilizations.name: Nubian Civilizations
civilizations.description: Nubian civilizations developed along the Nile south of Egypt and created powerful kingdoms with their own political, cultural and architectural traditions.
civilizations.legacy: Nubian kingdoms played an important role in the history of the Nile Valley and ancient Africa.

civilizations.name: Olmec Civilization
civilizations.description: The Olmec civilization developed in the Gulf Coast region of present-day Mexico and is known for monumental sculpture and early Mesoamerican cultural traditions.
civilizations.legacy: Olmec traditions are important to the study of early Mesoamerican civilization and cultural development.

civilizations.name: Classical Japanese Civilization
civilizations.description: Early Japanese civilization developed through evolving political institutions, cultural traditions, Buddhism, Shinto practices and court culture.
civilizations.legacy: Classical Japanese culture shaped later traditions in literature, architecture, religion, art and governance.
